events.summary: Egypt's military ruler Field Marshal Hussein Tantawi said presidential elections will be held by the end of June 2012 and that the military is prepared to hold a referendum on immediately transferring power to a civilian authority, a concession immediately rejected by protesters in Tahrir Square.
Both candidates in Egypt's presidential runoff claim victory amid protests in Tahrir Square over the military council's moves to retain power.
Millions of Egyptians vote in the first free presidential election in the country's history, with a runoff expected since no candidate is likely to win more than 50 percent.

Egypt's ruling generals issue an interim constitution that removes the military and the defense minister from presidential oversight and claims all legislative powers, after a court ordered the dissolution of the newly elected Parliament.
Mohammed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood is declared the winner of Egypt's first free presidential election, succeeding ousted President Hosni Mubarak.
Egyptian officials postpone announcing the winner of the disputed presidential runoff election between Mohammed Morsi and Ahmed Shafiq, citing the need to review about 400 complaints of voting fraud.

Egypt's military council, led by Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, met with political party heads and offered to speed up the transfer of power to an elected government by July 2012, while protesters in Tahrir Square rejected the offer and demanded the military step down immediately.
Mohamed Morsi is declared Egypt's first democratically elected president after winning 51% of the vote in the presidential runoff, defeating Ahmed Shafik.
Egypt holds its first free presidential election, with early counts showing Muslim Brotherhood candidate Mohammed Morsi leading and Ahmed Shafiq second, and no formal result announced until Tuesday.

A movement to boycott Egypt's runoff presidential election between Muslim Brotherhood candidate Mohamed Morsi and Ahmed Shafik, a holdover from Hosni Mubarak's government, gains momentum ahead of the vote.
Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court dissolves the Islamist-dominated parliament, ruling that one-third of its legislators were unlawfully elected.
Egypt's Supreme Presidential Election Commission is set to announce the results of the disputed presidential runoff between Muslim Brotherhood candidate Mohammed Morsi and Ahmed Shafiq.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government to discuss a vital $4.8 billion loan as the country battles a currency crisis.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government to discuss a vital $4.8 billion loan as the country battles a currency crisis.

The U.N. Security Council condemns the Syrian government in the strongest possible terms for heavy-weapon attacks on the town of Houla that killed 108 people, including 34 children, though the statement stops short of directly blaming any party and the Syrian government denies responsibility.

Egypt faces a potential currency crisis as the pound falls to record lows and households increasingly convert savings into dollars, with analysts warning that further household dollarization could wipe out the central bank's reserves.

Egypt announces it will reopen talks with the IMF next month on a $4.8 billion loan and lays out a revised economic reform programme including a stock market levy and a flat 25 percent corporate tax rate.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government to discuss a vital $4.8 billion loan as Egypt battles a currency crisis.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government for talks on a vital $4.8 billion loan as the country battles a currency crisis.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government to discuss a vital $4.8 billion loan as the country battles a currency crisis.
The Egyptian pound fell to a record low against the dollar as the central bank introduced a new dollar auction system and intervened to stabilize trading.

The International Monetary Fund says Egypt's financial situation is deteriorating and it will not move ahead with a $4.8 billion loan until it receives updated economic information and reform plans from President Mohammed Morsi's government.
Egypt delayed its request for a $4.8 billion IMF loan and suspended a package of tax hikes amid a political crisis over a disputed constitution, threatening to worsen the country's ailing economy.
Egypt's finance minister says a vital $4.8 billion IMF loan to Egypt will be delayed until next month as the political crisis deepens.

Egypt's Planning and Investment Minister Ashraf El-Arabi says Egypt is in an economic crisis from which it cannot recover without reaching a final accord with the IMF for a $4.8 billion loan, and that the government will invite the IMF back to Egypt within days.

Egyptian Prime Minister Hesham Kandil visited Gaza to show solidarity with Hamas and said Egypt would spare no effort to stop the Israeli aggression and achieve a truce, while Israel held its fire during the visit despite continued rocket attacks.
Israel and Hamas begin talks in Egypt on a truce, with Egypt working with both sides on negotiating new border arrangements for Gaza.

Egypt's President Mohamed Mursi says efforts to conclude a truce between the Palestinian and Israeli sides will produce positive results in the next few hours, as Egypt is brokered as a key player in ceasefire talks.
Egypt is taking the leading role in mediating between Israel and Hamas amid the Gaza crisis, with an Israeli envoy arriving in Cairo for ceasefire talks.

Egypt's President Mohamed Morsi helped negotiate a truce to end a week of conflict in Gaza, with US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton thanking him for his personal leadership in de-escalating the situation.

Egypt's new government, led by President Mohamed Morsi, responds to Israel's military offensive on Gaza by recalling Egypt's ambassador to Israel and calling on the UN Security Council to meet on the crisis, amid domestic pressure from the Muslim Brotherhood to sever ties with Israel.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy’s government continues to mediate negotiations toward a cease-fire in the Israel-Gaza conflict, with Hamas leader Khaled Meshaal visiting Cairo for talks and Morsy expressing tepid optimism that a cease-fire could be reached soon.
Egypt's military crackdown in the Sinai Peninsula severely disrupted smuggling tunnels to Gaza, causing fuel shortages and doubling building material prices.
Egypt's Islamist President Mohammed Morsi recalled Egypt's ambassador to Israel in protest of Israeli airstrikes on Gaza and ordered his prime minister to visit Gaza in a symbolic show of solidarity.

A dispute between Egypt and Gaza's Hamas government has produced the worst energy crisis in Gaza in years, with 18-hour-a-day blackouts and fuel shortages, as Egypt refuses to open a direct trade route with Gaza.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi condemns Israel's air strikes on Gaza as "a blatant aggression against humanity" and vows Cairo "would not leave Gaza on its own," amid protests in Cairo and Alexandria.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak resigns, prompting Israel to express hope that its peace accord with Egypt will remain unchanged while Hamas calls on Egypt's new leadership to lift the Gaza blockade.

events.summary: Egypt's opposition rejects the disputed draft constitution and calls for more street protests to try to force President Mohammed Morsi to abandon the referendum scheduled for Dec. 15.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy amended a law to limit voters to their own electoral districts ahead of a Saturday referendum on a controversial draft constitution, as competing demonstrations were held in Cairo and nine protesters were injured in an assault on Tahrir Square.

Egypt's main opposition coalition criticizes President Mohammed Morsi's decision to press ahead with a Dec. 15 referendum on a new constitution after rescinding his controversial Nov. 22 decree, saying it will deepen the political crisis.

Egypt's military and prosecutors arrest key Muslim Brotherhood leaders, including supreme guide Mohamed Badie, in a nationwide crackdown a day after the coup that toppled President Mohamed Morsi.

Egypt's President Mohamed Mursi says efforts to conclude a truce between the Palestinian and Israeli sides will produce positive results in the next few hours, as Egypt is brokered as a key player in ceasefire talks.

Egyptians are struggling to buy subsidized cooking gas as shortages force them to turn to the black market, while President Mohamed Mursi seeks to end the fuel shortage and reform Egypt's subsidy system.

The Muslim Brotherhood played a key role in the Egyptian revolution that ousted President Hosni Mubarak, positioning itself as a mainstream movement by supporting opposition groups and Mohamed ElBaradei.

Supporters and opponents of deposed Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi continue to hold rival rallies in Cairo as the military-backed transitional government moves forward without him or the Muslim Brotherhood.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi condemns Israel's air strikes on Gaza as "a blatant aggression against humanity" and vows Cairo "would not leave Gaza on its own," amid protests in Cairo and Alexandria.

facts.text: On 2012-03-29, Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood leadership met to discuss whether to enter a candidate in the upcoming May presidential elections, despite its earlier promises not to run.
On 2012-06-24, Mohammed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood was declared the winner of Egypt's first free presidential election, succeeding ousted President Hosni Mubarak.
On 2012-12-01, Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi called a 15 December referendum on a controversial draft constitution amid continued protests in Cairo's Tahrir Square.
On 2012-12-25, Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi signed into law a new Islamist-drafted constitution after it was approved in a referendum with 63.8 percent of the vote.
On 2013-01-29, Egypt's army chief warned that political unrest was pushing the state to the brink of collapse, as the death toll from five days of violence reached 52.

On 2013-06-30, hundreds of thousands of protesters across Egypt rallied to force President Mohammed Morsi from office, while his Islamist supporters vowed to defend him and clashes left at least four dead.
On 2013-07-03, Egypt's army ousted elected president Mohamed Morsi, suspended the constitution, and scheduled fresh elections, with Morsi reportedly held and at least 14 killed in clashes.

On 2013-07-08, Egyptian security forces opened fire on Muslim Brotherhood supporters outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo, killing at least 51 people, the worst violence since the military ousted President Mohamed Morsi.

event.summary: Egyptian military chief General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warns that the army will not stand by and allow Egypt to fall into a "dark tunnel of conflict," saying the army has a "moral responsibility" to prevent strife ahead of planned anti-government protests.
Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court dissolves the Islamist-dominated parliament, ruling that one-third of its legislators were unlawfully elected.
Britain revoked five export licenses to Egypt to prevent British goods from being used in unrest that has led to civilian deaths.

events.summary: An Egyptian court sentenced former president Hosni Mubarak to life in prison for complicity in the killing of protesters during the 2011 revolution, while acquitting him of corruption charges.
An Egyptian activist, Ahmed Douma, was convicted of insulting President Mohammed Morsi and spreading false news and given a six-month suspended sentence.

An Egyptian court sentences ousted President Hosni Mubarak and former Interior Minister Habib Adli to life in prison, while acquitting Mubarak's sons and the former interior minister's assistants, prompting thousands of protesters in Tahrir Square to demand a change to the verdict.
An Egyptian court acquits 12 activists opposed to ousted Islamist president Mohamed Morsi of charges they incited violence against members of his Muslim Brotherhood.

Egypt's new rulers announce that deposed President Mohamed Morsi is to be investigated over his escape from prison with 30 senior Muslim Brotherhood members during the 2011 uprising, signaling an intention to legally pursue him.
Egypt's top appeals court overturns the life sentence for former President Hosni Mubarak and orders a retrial over the killings of protesters during the 2011 uprising.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi declared a state of emergency and nighttime curfew across Port Said, Suez, and Ismailia for 30 days after three days of violence left nearly 50 dead and hundreds injured nationwide.

Egyptian prosecutors will investigate allegations that ousted president Mohammed Morsi and more than 30 other Muslim Brotherhood leaders escaped from prison during the 2011 revolution with help from Hamas.

Egypt's supreme constitutional court dissolves the Islamist-dominated parliament and rules that army-backed candidate Ahmed Shafiq can remain in the presidential race, a decision denounced as a coup by the Muslim Brotherhood and other opposition leaders.

A Saudi court sentenced Egyptian human rights lawyer el-Gezawi to five years in prison and 300 lashes for drug smuggling, a verdict his supporters say was politically motivated and based on a confession obtained under duress.

Prosecutors charge Gamal and Alaa Mubarak, sons of deposed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, with money laundering, while protests continue in Cairo's Tahrir Square over Mubarak's life sentence and the acquittal of six of his security officers.
A chaotic burst of dawn violence in Egypt leaves 51 civilians dead, further fracturing the country's national unity.
The Egyptian military overthrows President Mohamed Morsi after mass protests.
Israel reportedly threatened to strike militants in the Sinai if Egypt fails to secure the shared border, amid tensions following rocket fire into Eilat and repeated attacks on a gas pipeline.
Egypt's Interior Ministry raises the state of emergency for police in the Sinai peninsula after receiving intelligence that jihadist groups might attack their forces there.

The Egyptian army sent reinforcements into the Sinai Peninsula after President Mohammad Mursi said there would be no talks with militant Islamists who abducted seven members of the security forces last week.
Suspected militants in Egypt's Sinai abducted seven Egyptian security personnel as they headed to Cairo for holidays, the first such kidnapping of security forces in the lawless peninsula.
Egypt's military ousts former president Mohamed Morsi, prompting Israel to closely monitor the unrest and its potential spillover effects.

A new Islamist group, Ansar al-Shariah in Egypt, announces its formation and threatens violence in response to the army's ousting of President Mohamed Mursi, which it calls a declaration of war on its faith.
Egypt's Islamist President Mohammed Morsi recalled Egypt's ambassador to Israel in protest of Israeli airstrikes on Gaza and ordered his prime minister to visit Gaza in a symbolic show of solidarity.
Israel's military says Egypt has moved forces into the border area near the Gaza Strip in coordination with Israel, as an army ultimatum to President Mohammed Morsi nears.
Egypt deploys 1,500 additional troops in the Sinai peninsula, a move coordinated with Israeli security forces.
Armed militants attacked an Egyptian security post near the border with Israel and Gaza, killing at least 16 Egyptian soldiers during Ramadan iftar.

The death toll from Egypt's uprising reaches at least 75 over a chaotic week, with over 1,079 injured amid violence in Cairo, Alexandria, and other cities, as a newly formed militant group Ansar al-Shariah arms itself and brands the military coup a "war against Islam."

At least 29 people are killed as Muslim Brotherhood supporters clash with opponents of ousted President Mohammed Morsi across Egypt, including fatal shootings outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo.
Millions of Egyptians vote in the first free presidential election in the country's history, with a runoff expected since no candidate is likely to win more than 50 percent.
At least 17 people died across Egypt as Islamists opposed to the overthrow of President Mohamed Mursi took to the streets to protest what they say was a military coup.

Egypt's military-backed interim president dissolves the Islamist-dominated upper house of parliament as soldiers open fire on mostly Islamist protesters in Cairo demanding the restoration of ousted President Mohammed Morsi, killing at least one person.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi met with army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and cabinet ministers to discuss stabilizing the nation after clashes between his supporters and opponents outside the presidential palace, as the Republican Guard deployed tanks and set a 3 P.M. deadline for protesters to evacuate the area.

events.summary: Egypt's military, led by Defense Minister Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, dismissed elected President Mohamed Morsi, dissolved parliament, and suspended the constitution, a move Morsi's supporters denounced as a military coup.
Egypt's chief justice Adly al-Mansour is sworn in as interim president after the army ousted and detained Mohamed Morsi.

Egypt's military-installed government wavered on appointing Mohamed ElBaradei as interim prime minister, with state media and his office announcing his selection before the government backtracked hours later, saying no final decision had been made.

Egypt's public prosecutor orders the assets of 14 Muslim Brotherhood members, including its head Mohamed Badie, to be frozen, while army chief Abdel Fattah al-Sisi says no group will be barred from participating in politics.
The United States cautiously welcomes Egypt's interim government plan to hold quick parliamentary and presidential elections, while avoiding whether a military coup had occurred.
Mohamed Morsi is declared the winner of Egypt's presidential runoff, becoming the country's first freely elected president.
An Islamist leader wins the Egyptian presidency.

The Muslim Brotherhood declares its candidate, Mohammed Morsi, won Egypt's presidential election, while the military issues an interim constitution granting itself sweeping powers over the new president.

Egyptian military chief General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warns that the army will not stand by and allow Egypt to fall into a "dark tunnel of conflict," saying the army has a "moral responsibility" to prevent strife ahead of planned anti-government protests.

Egypt's interim president swears in the first Cabinet since the military ousted Islamist president Mohammed Morsi, led by Prime Minister Hazem el-Beblawi and including three women but no Islamist figures.

Egyptian voters approve a disputed, Islamist-backed constitution with 63.8 percent support amid a 32.9 percent turnout, after which President Mohammed Morsi signs a decree putting the new constitution into effect.

Preliminary results released by the Muslim Brotherhood show that Egypt's disputed Islamist-backed constitution received a "yes" majority of more than 70 percent in the second and final round of voting on the referendum, with a turnout of about 30 percent.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy amended a law to limit voters to their own electoral districts ahead of a Saturday referendum on a controversial draft constitution, as competing demonstrations were held in Cairo and nine protesters were injured in an assault on Tahrir Square.

The first round of Egypt's national referendum on a proposed constitution, which is expected to be approved but is likely to deepen divisions, is held in 10 governorates including Alexandria and half of Cairo.

Egyptians vote in a referendum on a controversial Islamist-backed constitution that has polarized the nation, with President Morsi and his Islamist supporters backing the charter while liberals, secular Muslims and Christians oppose it.
Egypt holds its first parliamentary elections since the fall of Hosni Mubarak, with a high turnout and voting reported as mostly peaceful.
Egypt begins the first stage of its parliamentary election in nine provinces, with voter turnout estimated above 70% and Islamists expecting gains.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood claims the Islamist-backed constitution passed with a 64 percent "yes" vote, though the opposition alleges irregularities and may contest the outcome.

Egypt's opposition National Salvation Front says it will appeal the two-stage referendum on a new constitution backed by ruling Islamists, alleging polling fraud and violations, and calls for an investigation before official results are announced.
Egypt's opposition rejects the disputed draft constitution and calls for more street protests to try to force President Mohammed Morsi to abandon the referendum scheduled for Dec. 15.

Egypt's tourism minister Hesham Zazou resigned over the government appointment of Adel Mohammed Al-Khayat, an Islamic fundamentalist linked to the group behind the 1997 Luxor massacre, as governor of Luxor province.
Hosni Mubarak suffers a stroke and undergoes defibrillation in prison before being transferred to a military hospital.

Egypt's armed forces chief Abdel Fattah al-Sisi says the military is ready to die to defend the people against "terrorists" and extremists, after President Mohamed Mursi rejected an army ultimatum and public pressure to quit.

Egypt's military, led by defence minister Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, issues a 48-hour ultimatum calling for an inclusive political process to end the rift between President Mohammed Morsi's Muslim Brotherhood and its opponents, without itself directly entering politics or government.
Mohamed ElBaradei is named prime minister of Egypt's new interim government following the military coup against President Mohamed Morsi.
The Egyptian military stays out of Egypt's latest political crisis, saying it has returned to its natural role of protecting the nation and would only intervene if called upon.

existing_events.summary: At least 26 people are killed and more than 850 wounded in clashes across Egypt between supporters and opponents of ousted President Mohamed Morsy, and Egyptian authorities arrest Muslim Brotherhood deputy supreme leader Khairat el-Shater.

The death toll from Egypt's uprising reaches at least 75 over a chaotic week, with over 1,079 injured amid violence in Cairo, Alexandria, and other cities, as a newly formed militant group Ansar al-Shariah arms itself and brands the military coup a "war against Islam."

At least 29 people are killed as Muslim Brotherhood supporters clash with opponents of ousted President Mohammed Morsi across Egypt, including fatal shootings outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo.
President Obama says he is deeply concerned about the Egyptian military's overthrow of President Mohamed Morsi but avoids calling it a coup, which would trigger automatic cuts in U.S. aid to Egypt.
Egypt's military and prosecutors arrest key Muslim Brotherhood leaders, including supreme guide Mohamed Badie, in a nationwide crackdown a day after the coup that toppled President Mohamed Morsi.

Egypt's army ousts elected president Mohamed Morsi, suspends the constitution, and schedules fresh elections, with Morsi reportedly held by authorities in an unknown location and at least 14 people killed in clashes after the announcement.
Egypt's chief justice Adly al-Mansour is sworn in as interim president after the army ousted and detained Mohamed Morsi.
Egyptian military authorities arrested Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Badie in Marsa Matrouh as part of a crackdown following the removal of President Mohammed Morsi.

events.summary: Egyptians are set to begin voting in a divisive referendum on a new constitution drafted by an Islamist-dominated assembly, which opponents including Christians, secularists and women criticize as exclusionary.
Egypt's opposition rejects the disputed draft constitution and calls for more street protests to try to force President Mohammed Morsi to abandon the referendum scheduled for Dec. 15.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi calls a 15 December referendum on a controversial draft constitution amid continued protests in Cairo's Tahrir Square.

Egyptians voted narrowly in favor of a controversial new constitution backed by President Mohammed Morsi, amid accusations of widespread ballot box violations and calls by rights groups for a repeat of the first round of the referendum.
Egyptians vote in a referendum on a disputed constitution drafted by Islamist supporters of President Mohammed Morsi, which has polarized the nation.

Egypt's constitution-writing assembly begins voting on a final draft, a move Muslim Brotherhood allies of President Mohamed Mursi hope will help end the crisis prompted by his decree expanding his powers.

Egyptians are voting in the second round of a referendum on a disputed draft constitution that has polarized the country and plunged it into its worst crisis since the ouster of President Hosni Mubarak.
The Egyptian people voted in a referendum proposed by the army on several constitutional amendments.

Egyptians vote in a referendum on a controversial Islamist-backed constitution that has polarized the nation, with President Morsi and his Islamist supporters backing the charter while liberals, secular Muslims and Christians oppose it.
Voters begin casting ballots in Egypt on a new constitution in a referendum marred by power plays, division, and violent protests.

Egypt's main opposition coalition criticizes President Mohammed Morsi's decision to press ahead with a Dec. 15 referendum on a new constitution after rescinding his controversial Nov. 22 decree, saying it will deepen the political crisis.
Egypt's opposition calls on its followers to vote "no" in a referendum on a disputed constitution drafted by Islamist supporters of President Mohammed Morsi.
An Egyptian activist, Ahmed Douma, was convicted of insulting President Mohammed Morsi and spreading false news and given a six-month suspended sentence.

Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak was sentenced to life in prison for failing to stop the killing of protesters during Egypt's uprising, while he and his sons were acquitted of corruption charges.

Egypt's new rulers announce that deposed President Mohamed Morsi is to be investigated over his escape from prison with 30 senior Muslim Brotherhood members during the 2011 uprising, signaling an intention to legally pursue him.

In Alexandria, Muslim Brotherhood supporters threw three teenage boys off a roof during clashes, killing 17-year-old Hamada Badr, amid nationwide protests against the military's removal of President Mohamed Morsi.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi declared a state of emergency and nighttime curfew across Port Said, Suez, and Ismailia for 30 days after three days of violence left nearly 50 dead and hundreds injured nationwide.
The Tamarod campaign says more than 22 million people have signed a petition demanding President Mohamed Morsi's resignation and a snap election, ahead of planned opposition protests.
Egypt's highest court postponed its ruling on the legitimacy of the constitutional assembly after judges accused Islamist supporters of President Mohamed Morsi of blocking their chambers.

Egypt's supreme constitutional court dissolves the Islamist-dominated parliament and rules that army-backed candidate Ahmed Shafiq can remain in the presidential race, a decision denounced as a coup by the Muslim Brotherhood and other opposition leaders.

Egypt's stock market plunges nearly 10 percent and violent protests erupt over President Morsi's decree expanding his powers and shielding his decisions from judicial review, with one teenager killed and more than 500 injured in clashes.
A mother and her seven children are sentenced to 15 years in jail in Egypt for converting back to Christianity from Islam.
Hosni Mubarak's retrial for alleged complicity in the killings of 2011 protesters resumed, with his lawyers entering a not guilty plea, and the court adjourned proceedings until August 17.
A chaotic burst of dawn violence in Egypt leaves 51 civilians dead, further fracturing the country's national unity.

Hosni Mubarak suffers a stroke and undergoes defibrillation in prison before being transferred to a military hospital.
Egyptian officials postpone announcing the winner of the disputed presidential runoff election between Mohammed Morsi and Ahmed Shafiq, citing the need to review about 400 complaints of voting fraud.
Mohammed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood is declared the winner of Egypt's first free presidential election, succeeding ousted President Hosni Mubarak.

Tens of thousands of Egyptians celebrate in Cairo's Tahrir Square after Mohamed Morsi is declared the winner of Egypt's presidential election, though official results confirming Morsi as the next president were announced the following day.
An Islamist leader wins the Egyptian presidency.
Insecurity and armed attacks on police and army are on the rise in Egypt's North Sinai, a restive flashpoint region that shares borders with both Israel and the Gaza Strip.

Egypt's judges demand that President Mohammed Morsi reverse his decision to reinstate parliament within 36 hours or face "painful measures," after the Supreme Constitutional Court said its ruling to dissolve the lower house was irreversible.
Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court freezes President Mohamed Morsi's decree reinstating the Islamist-led parliament, hours after the lower house convened in defiance of the judiciary and military.
Armed militants attacked an Egyptian security post near the border with Israel and Gaza, killing at least 16 Egyptian soldiers during Ramadan iftar.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood blames the Sinai attack that killed 16 policemen on Mossad, while Israel's Foreign Ministry denies the claims.
Egyptian army helicopters strike jihadist encampments inside Sinai, reportedly killing twenty of them.
Clashes broke out in Cairo between pro-Morsi and anti-Morsi protesters after Friday prayer, with rocks thrown and crowds fleeing toward Talaat Harb Square.

Protests occur at the U.S. Embassy in Cairo, Egypt, where demonstrators breach the walls, tear down the American flag, and replace it with a black Islamic flag, amid violent protests in the Middle East over an amateur film thought to insult Mohammed.
Israel rejects Egypt's calls to amend the 1979 peace treaty's limits on troops in the Sinai, with Foreign Minister Avigdor Lieberman saying there is no chance Israel will agree to any change.

Egyptians are struggling to buy subsidized cooking gas as shortages force them to turn to the black market, while President Mohamed Mursi seeks to end the fuel shortage and reform Egypt's subsidy system.

Egypt's new government, led by President Mohamed Morsi, responds to Israel's military offensive on Gaza by recalling Egypt's ambassador to Israel and calling on the UN Security Council to meet on the crisis, amid domestic pressure from the Muslim Brotherhood to sever ties with Israel.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi condemns Israel's air strikes on Gaza as "a blatant aggression against humanity" and vows Cairo "would not leave Gaza on its own," amid protests in Cairo and Alexandria.

Egyptian Prime Minister Hesham Kandil visited Gaza to show solidarity with Hamas and said Egypt would spare no effort to stop the Israeli aggression and achieve a truce, while Israel held its fire during the visit despite continued rocket attacks.
Egypt is taking the leading role in mediating between Israel and Hamas amid the Gaza crisis, with an Israeli envoy arriving in Cairo for ceasefire talks.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy’s government continues to mediate negotiations toward a cease-fire in the Israel-Gaza conflict, with Hamas leader Khaled Meshaal visiting Cairo for talks and Morsy expressing tepid optimism that a cease-fire could be reached soon.

Egypt's President Mohamed Mursi says efforts to conclude a truce between the Palestinian and Israeli sides will produce positive results in the next few hours, as Egypt is brokered as a key player in ceasefire talks.

Egypt's President Mohamed Morsi helped negotiate a truce to end a week of conflict in Gaza, with US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton thanking him for his personal leadership in de-escalating the situation.

Egypt's stock market plunges nearly 10 percent and violent protests erupt over President Morsi's decree expanding his powers and shielding his decisions from judicial review, with one teenager killed and more than 500 injured in clashes.
The Muslim Brotherhood office is attacked.
The Egyptian military stays out of Egypt's latest political crisis, saying it has returned to its natural role of protecting the nation and would only intervene if called upon.
Egyptian President Mohammed Morsi meets with senior judges to defuse a mounting crisis over his assumption of sweeping new powers, which has sparked deadly protests and a showdown with the judiciary.
Israel and Hamas begin talks in Egypt on a truce, with Egypt working with both sides on negotiating new border arrangements for Gaza.
Tens of thousands of protesters are due to stage a mass rally against Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi in Cairo's Tahrir Square amid growing public anger over his power grab.
More than 200,000 people packed Cairo's Tahrir Square to protest against Islamist President Mohammed Morsi, demanding he rescind decrees granting him near-absolute powers.
A protester against Mohammed Morsi dies after inhaling tear gas fired by Egyptian police during clashes in Cairo, as protests continue over Morsi's decree expanding his powers.
Egypt's two highest appeals courts suspend their work in protest over presidential decrees granting Mohammed Morsi nearly absolute powers.

Hundreds of demonstrators remain in Cairo's Tahrir Square for a sixth day demanding that President Mohamed Mursi rescind a decree they say gives him dictatorial powers, while two of Egypt's top courts suspend work in protest.

Egypt's highest appeals court suspends work and the Supreme Constitutional Court accuses President Mohamed Morsi of attacking the justice system in protest of his edict granting him power to legislate without judicial oversight.

Egypt's constituent assembly begins voting on a final draft constitution as President Mohamed Mursi is expected to call for national unity in a public address amid a political crisis over his sweeping powers.
Tens of thousands of Egyptians protest against President Mohamed Mursi after an Islamist-led assembly approved a new draft constitution, with clashes reported in Alexandria and Al-Mahala Al-Kobra.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi calls a 15 December referendum on a controversial draft constitution amid continued protests in Cairo's Tahrir Square.
Thousands of Islamists rally in Cairo in support of President Mohamed Morsi and the constitution he is promoting, as opposition protests and clashes continue over his newly expanded powers.
Egypt's highest court postponed its ruling on the legitimacy of the constitutional assembly after judges accused Islamist supporters of President Mohamed Morsi of blocking their chambers.

Thousands of Egyptians protest outside the presidential palace in Cairo, escalating pressure on President Mohamed Morsi to rescind the decree granting himself far-reaching powers, with sporadic clashes with security forces using tear gas.

Supporters and opponents of Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi fought pitched battles outside the presidential palace after the vice president vowed that a referendum on the controversial draft constitution would go ahead as scheduled.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi met with army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and cabinet ministers to discuss stabilizing the nation after clashes between his supporters and opponents outside the presidential palace, as the Republican Guard deployed tanks and set a 3 P.M. deadline for protesters to evacuate the area.

As protests against Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi continue for a fourth day, Morsi turns to the Muslim Brotherhood and his Islamist base, offering a possible delay in the Dec. 15 constitutional referendum while opposition leaders reject his concessions.

Egyptians are set to begin voting in a divisive referendum on a new constitution drafted by an Islamist-dominated assembly, which opponents including Christians, secularists and women criticize as exclusionary.
Egypt's opposition rejects the disputed draft constitution and calls for more street protests to try to force President Mohammed Morsi to abandon the referendum scheduled for Dec. 15.

Egypt's main opposition coalition criticizes President Mohammed Morsi's decision to press ahead with a Dec. 15 referendum on a new constitution after rescinding his controversial Nov. 22 decree, saying it will deepen the political crisis.

Egypt's opposition National Salvation Front urges continued protests against the December 15 constitutional referendum, calling for another mass demonstration on Tuesday while stopping short of advocating a boycott or "no" vote.

A decree by Egyptian President Mohammed Morsi giving the military temporary authority to arrest civilians and protect vital state facilities takes effect, lasting until the results of the scheduled constitutional referendum are announced.
Egypt delayed its request for a $4.8 billion IMF loan and suspended a package of tax hikes amid a political crisis over a disputed constitution, threatening to worsen the country's ailing economy.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy amended a law to limit voters to their own electoral districts ahead of a Saturday referendum on a controversial draft constitution, as competing demonstrations were held in Cairo and nine protesters were injured in an assault on Tahrir Square.

Egypt's army chief hosts national unity talks to seek an end to the political and economic crisis, with President Mohamed Mursi and the Muslim Brotherhood expected to attend while the main opposition coalition said it would decide whether to participate.
Egypt's opposition calls on its followers to vote "no" in a referendum on a disputed constitution drafted by Islamist supporters of President Mohammed Morsi.

Egyptians voted narrowly in favor of a controversial new constitution backed by President Mohammed Morsi, amid accusations of widespread ballot box violations and calls by rights groups for a repeat of the first round of the referendum.

Egyptians vote in a referendum on a controversial Islamist-backed constitution that has polarized the nation, with President Morsi and his Islamist supporters backing the charter while liberals, secular Muslims and Christians oppose it.
Egyptians vote in the second round of a referendum on a disputed draft constitution that has polarized the country and plunged it into its worst crisis since the ouster of President Hosni Mubarak.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood claims the Islamist-backed constitution passed with a 64 percent "yes" vote, though the opposition alleges irregularities and may contest the outcome.

Egypt's opposition National Salvation Front says it will appeal the two-stage referendum on a new constitution backed by ruling Islamists, alleging polling fraud and violations, and calls for an investigation before official results are announced.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi signs into law a new Islamist-drafted constitution after it was approved in a referendum with 63.8 percent of the vote.
The Egyptian pound fell to a record low against the dollar as the central bank introduced a new dollar auction system and intervened to stabilize trading.

A high-level Egyptian delegation including the intelligence chief flew to the United Arab Emirates to discuss the case of imprisoned Egyptians and to ease escalating tensions between Egypt and the U.A.E.
A senior IMF official meets Egypt's government to discuss a vital $4.8 billion loan as the country battles a currency crisis.
Egyptian troops foiled a bomb attack on a church in Rafah timed to coincide with Coptic Orthodox Christmas.

Egypt faces a potential currency crisis as the pound falls to record lows and households increasingly convert savings into dollars, with analysts warning that further household dollarization could wipe out the central bank's reserves.
Egypt's currency crisis has intensified its oil supply troubles, with state-owned EGPC purchasing only half of the crude oil it sought in a tender and facing difficulties obtaining letters of credit.

Egypt's central bank introduced a new foreign exchange system, including dollar auctions, to curb speculation and protect reserves, as the Egyptian pound fell to a record low near 6.4 to the U.S. dollar.
Egypt's top appeals court overturns the life sentence for former President Hosni Mubarak and orders a retrial over the killings of protesters during the 2011 uprising.

A Saudi court sentenced Egyptian human rights lawyer el-Gezawi to five years in prison and 300 lashes for drug smuggling, a verdict his supporters say was politically motivated and based on a confession obtained under duress.
A mother and her seven children are sentenced to 15 years in jail in Egypt for converting back to Christianity from Islam.

Two years after the uprising that ousted Hosni Mubarak, many remnants of the old regime have evaded jail time and continue to lead comfortable lives, with only two of nearly 170 police officers charged with killing about 900 protesters during the 2011 uprising in prison.
At least 32 people were killed in Port Said when Egyptians rampaged in protest at the sentencing of 21 people to death over a soccer stadium disaster.
An Egyptian court sentences 21 people to death over a 2012 soccer riot in Port Said that killed 74 people, mostly Al-Ahly fans.
Egypt's President Mohammed Morsi declared a state of emergency and a 30-day curfew in the Suez Canal provinces of Port Said, Ismailiya, and Suez after weekend unrest left more than 50 people dead.
Egypt's President Mohammed Morsi declares a state of emergency and imposes a 30-day curfew in the Suez Canal provinces of Port Said, Ismailiya, and Suez after weekend unrest left more than 50 dead.

Egyptian protesters defied a nighttime curfew in restive towns along the Suez Canal, attacking police stations and ignoring emergency rule imposed by Islamist President Mohamed Mursi to end days of clashes that have killed at least 52 people.
Egypt's army chief warned that political unrest is pushing the state to the brink of collapse, as the death toll from five days of violence reached 52.
Egyptian authorities scaled back a curfew imposed by President Mohamed Mursi, and Mursi cut short a visit to Europe to deal with the deadliest violence in the seven months since he took power.

Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rate climbed to 6.3 percent in January from 4.7 percent in December, the biggest increase in more than two years, as the pound weakened to a record and foreign reserves slid.
An Egyptian man shot during protests in Cairo died of his wounds, raising the death toll in the bloodiest week of President Mohamed Mursi's seven months in power to 57.
An Egyptian protester, Mohamed el-Guindy, dies after allegedly being beaten and strangled for four days by police, prompting President Mohamed Morsi to announce an investigation into his death.

Egypt's powerful military signals growing impatience with Islamist President Mohammed Morsi and his Muslim Brotherhood group, indirectly criticizing their policies and issuing thinly veiled threats that it might seize power again.

Egypt's Planning and Investment Minister Ashraf El-Arabi says Egypt is in an economic crisis from which it cannot recover without reaching a final accord with the IMF for a $4.8 billion loan, and that the government will invite the IMF back to Egypt within days.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi calls parliamentary elections for April.

Egypt announces it will reopen talks with the IMF next month on a $4.8 billion loan and lays out a revised economic reform programme including a stock market levy and a flat 25 percent corporate tax rate.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry releases $250 million in economic aid to Egypt, including $190 million for the government budget and $60 million for an Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund, with additional support contingent on President Mohamed Morsy implementing economic and political reforms.
Egypt's military intervened in clashes between thousands of protesters and police in Port Said, forming a line between the two sides, in violence that killed two security members and two civilians.

Egypt faces economic crisis and potential social unrest over whether to accept an IMF loan requiring subsidy reforms, with foreign currency reserves falling to $13.5 billion and warnings of a "revolution of the hungry."

Thousands of low-ranking Egyptian policemen strike across Egypt for a fourth day, refusing orders to work and protesting what they claim is the politicization of the force in favor of President Mohammed Morsi's Muslim Brotherhood party.
Egypt's Interior Ministry raises the state of emergency for police in the Sinai peninsula after receiving intelligence that jihadist groups might attack their forces there.
Egyptian inflation rose to 8.2 percent year-on-year in February as the sliding pound pushed up food prices, hurting the poor amid the country's economic, political and security crisis.
Hundreds of truck and minibus drivers in Egypt block major roads and bridges in Cairo and highways across the country in protest over diesel fuel shortages.

Egyptian President Mohamed Mursi threatened to take unspecified measures to "protect this nation" after violent demonstrations against his Muslim Brotherhood, remarks the opposition said heralded a crackdown.
Ties between Egyptian President Mohamed Mursi and Egypt’s military leaders are described as being on a downswing amid tensions over the defense minister and the military’s role.
Egypt's state prosecutors ordered the arrest of popular television satirist Bassem Youssef for allegedly insulting Islam and President Mohammed Morsi.
A technical delegation from the International Monetary Fund arrives in Cairo for a new round of talks over a $4.8 billion loan.
An International Monetary Fund team resumed long-delayed negotiations with Egypt on a $4.8 billion loan to ease a deepening economic crisis.
Qatar pledged another $3 billion in aid to Egypt, extending the lifeline for Islamist President Mohamed Mursi after repeated delays in loan talks with the International Monetary Fund.
IMF officials are in Cairo negotiating conditions for a proposed $4.8bn loan to Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood government, amid protests and concerns over subsidy cuts and the government's legitimacy.
Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, his two sons, and his former interior minister are set to be retried.

The International Monetary Fund says Egypt's financial situation is deteriorating and it will not move ahead with a $4.8 billion loan until it receives updated economic information and reform plans from President Mohammed Morsi's government.

The retrial of former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak resumed, with prosecutors requesting to present new evidence from a fact-finding commission's report claiming Mubarak had full knowledge of the violence used against protesters.
Egypt's private security industry is growing amid post-revolution economic slump and crime wave, with firms like Firewall Security Consultants and Securitas expanding operations.
Suspected militants in Egypt's Sinai abducted seven Egyptian security personnel as they headed to Cairo for holidays, the first such kidnapping of security forces in the lawless peninsula.

The Egyptian army sent reinforcements into the Sinai Peninsula after President Mohammad Mursi said there would be no talks with militant Islamists who abducted seven members of the security forces last week.

Egyptian cement and brick makers have been hit by government cuts to energy subsidies, with gas prices rising at least 75 percent and fuel oil prices up 50 percent since February, as part of a four-year plan to remove industrial energy subsidies.

Egypt plans to cut natural gas exports and ask major industries to slow output in summer to avoid an energy crisis and stave off political unrest, according to the chairman of the Egyptian General Petroleum Company.
Egypt's military crackdown in the Sinai Peninsula severely disrupted smuggling tunnels to Gaza, causing fuel shortages and doubling building material prices.
An Egyptian activist, Ahmed Douma, was convicted of insulting President Mohammed Morsi and spreading false news and given a six-month suspended sentence.

An Egyptian court convicts foreign nonprofit workers, including 16 Americans, of operating unlicensed NGOs and sentences them to prison terms of one to five years, though most are unlikely to serve time.
Egypt's state prosecutor refers twelve prominent bloggers and activists to trial on charges of instigating violence during a March 22 demonstration against the Muslim Brotherhood.

Egypt's President Mohammed Morsi says Egypt will defend each drop of the Nile with its blood amid tensions over Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance dam, while also saying dialogue is the best means of solving the crisis.
A large Egyptian opposition movement accuses President Mohamed Mursi of having no plan for dealing with Ethiopia’s plan to build a dam that could siphon off vital Nile River water.

Egypt's largest opposition grouping says President Mohammed Mursi's calls for national reconciliation talks come "too late," as activists plan mass anti-Mursi rallies on June 30, the one-year anniversary of his inauguration.

Egypt's foreign minister visits Ethiopia to defuse a diplomatic standoff over Nile River water access after Ethiopia's parliament voted to strip Egypt of its right to the lion's share of Nile waters and Ethiopia vowed to proceed with a controversial dam.

Egypt's tourism minister Hesham Zazou resigned over the government appointment of Adel Mohammed Al-Khayat, an Islamic fundamentalist linked to the group behind the 1997 Luxor massacre, as governor of Luxor province.

The Rebel campaign is collecting signatures and planning nationwide protests to demand early presidential elections and declare President Mohamed Morsi's presidency unconstitutional ahead of his first anniversary in office.
Egypt announces a criminal investigation of deposed Islamist President Mohamed Mursi, with prosecutors examining complaints of spying, inciting violence and ruining the economy.

Egyptian military chief General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warns that the army will not stand by and allow Egypt to fall into a "dark tunnel of conflict," saying the army has a "moral responsibility" to prevent strife ahead of planned anti-government protests.

Egypt's ruling Muslim Brotherhood claims one man was shot dead and four wounded in an attack on a provincial party office in Zagazig, ahead of mass rallies calling for President Mohamed Mursi to resign.

Two people, including an American, were killed when protesters stormed an office of Egypt's ruling Muslim Brotherhood in Alexandria, amid growing tension ahead of mass rallies aimed at unseating President Mohamed Mursi.

Anti-Morsi protesters set fire to the Muslim Brotherhood headquarters and gun battles and street fighting left at least four people dead and more than 200 injured as the opposition's anti-government insurrection began.
Hundreds of Islamists gather in Cairo to show support for President Mohamed Morsi ahead of expected massive anti-Morsi protests on the first anniversary of his inauguration.
Mass demonstrations are planned across Egypt to demand the removal of President Mohamed Mursi, with fears of violence as the army says it will step in if unrest gets out of control.
The Tamarod campaign says more than 22 million people have signed a petition demanding President Mohamed Morsi's resignation and a snap election, ahead of planned opposition protests.
Hundreds of thousands of protesters across Egypt rally to force President Mohammed Morsi from office, while his Islamist supporters vow to defend him and clashes leave at least four dead.

Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi rejects opposition calls for early presidential elections and vows there will be no second revolution, setting the stage for mass protests and a trial of strength on the streets.
Egypt's presidency rejects an army ultimatum threatening to intervene if President Mohamed Morsi did not meet the demands of the people within 48 hours.
Six people were killed in unrest as protesters flooded Egypt's streets calling for Islamist President Mohamed Morsi to step down, the health ministry said.

Egypt's military, led by defence minister Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, issues a 48-hour ultimatum calling for an inclusive political process to end the rift between President Mohammed Morsi's Muslim Brotherhood and its opponents, without itself directly entering politics or government.
Egypt's armed forces give President Mohamed Mursi and feuding politicians 48 hours to compromise and share power, warning that otherwise the army will impose its own road map for the country.
Israel's military says Egypt has moved forces into the border area near the Gaza Strip in coordination with Israel, as an army ultimatum to President Mohammed Morsi nears.

Egypt's military-backed interim president appointed a veteran economist as prime minister and Mohamed ElBaradei as vice president, while the army warned political factions against impeding the transition.
Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi rebuffs an army ultimatum to resolve Egypt's political crisis, as ministers resign and the opposition refuses to talk.
Egypt's President Mohamed Morsi refuses to step down, rejecting an army ultimatum to form a coalition government by the next day or face a military-imposed solution.
A national crisis is unfolding in Egypt as the Egyptian masses demand the removal of the fundamentalist administration led by Morsi.

Egypt's armed forces draft a political roadmap to suspend the constitution and dissolve the Islamist-dominated parliament if President Mohamed Mursi and his opponents fail to reach a power-sharing agreement by Wednesday.
Egyptian military authorities arrested Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Badie in Marsa Matrouh as part of a crackdown following the removal of President Mohammed Morsi.
President Obama says he is deeply concerned about the Egyptian military's overthrow of President Mohamed Morsi but avoids calling it a coup, which would trigger automatic cuts in U.S. aid to Egypt.

Egypt's army ousts elected president Mohamed Morsi, suspends the constitution, and schedules fresh elections, with Morsi reportedly held by authorities in an unknown location and at least 14 people killed in clashes after the announcement.
Human Rights Watch reports that mobs sexually assaulted and in some cases raped at least 91 women in Cairo's Tahrir Square during four days of protests against President Mohamed Morsi.

The U.S. State Department says it is "very concerned" about the situation in Egypt amid sweeping protests and a stand-off between Egypt's armed forces and Islamist President Mohamed Morsi, and cannot confirm whether a military coup is underway.

Egypt's armed forces chief Abdel Fattah al-Sisi says the military is ready to die to defend the people against "terrorists" and extremists, after President Mohamed Mursi rejected an army ultimatum and public pressure to quit.

Egypt's top prosecutor opens an investigation into Mohamed Morsy and top Muslim Brotherhood leaders for allegedly inciting violence and the killing of protesters, and prevents Morsy and 35 others from leaving the country, while the military arrests Brotherhood leaders including Mohamed Badei and Mohamed Mahdi Akef.

The ouster of Egyptian president Mohamed Mursi raises hopes among businessmen and economists that Egypt's economy can escape its downward spiral, as the stock market jumps 7.3 percent and bond prices rise.

Supporters of ousted Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi gather at Cairo's Rabaa al Adawiya mosque, expressing rage at the military coup and chanting against military rule, as 300 arrest warrants are issued for Muslim Brotherhood members.
Egypt's military and prosecutors arrest key Muslim Brotherhood leaders, including supreme guide Mohamed Badie, in a nationwide crackdown a day after the coup that toppled President Mohamed Morsi.
Egypt's chief justice Adly al-Mansour is sworn in as interim president after the army ousted and detained Mohamed Morsi.
Egypt's military ousts President Mohamed Morsi, a move described as a soft coup that ends democratic rule and returns the military to the center of Egyptian politics.
The Egyptian military ousts President Mohamed Morsi, suspends the constitution, and appoints the head of the constitutional court as interim head of state amid violent protests.
At least 17 people died across Egypt as Islamists opposed to the overthrow of President Mohamed Mursi took to the streets to protest what they say was a military coup.
A wounded Muslim Brotherhood supporter describes seeing fellow protesters shot and killed by Egyptian security forces outside the Rabaa al-Adiwiya mosque in Cairo.
Gunfire erupts during Muslim Brotherhood protests in Cairo following the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi, with Reuters reporting three killed.

At least 26 people are killed and more than 850 wounded in clashes across Egypt between supporters and opponents of ousted President Mohamed Morsy, and Egyptian authorities arrest Muslim Brotherhood deputy supreme leader Khairat el-Shater.

In Alexandria, Islamist attackers killed 19-year-old Hamada Badr and wounded several other teenagers who had been chanting against the Muslim Brotherhood, amid violence following the army's deposition of President Mohamed Morsi.

The death toll from Egypt's uprising reaches at least 75 over a chaotic week, with over 1,079 injured amid violence in Cairo, Alexandria, and other cities, as a newly formed militant group Ansar al-Shariah arms itself and brands the military coup a "war against Islam."

Egypt's military-backed interim president dissolves the Islamist-dominated upper house of parliament as soldiers open fire on mostly Islamist protesters in Cairo demanding the restoration of ousted President Mohammed Morsi, killing at least one person.

At least 29 people are killed as Muslim Brotherhood supporters clash with opponents of ousted President Mohammed Morsi across Egypt, including fatal shootings outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo.
Gunmen shot dead Coptic Christian priest Mina Aboud Sharween in Egypt's Northern Sinai, in what could be the first sectarian attack since the military overthrow of Islamist President Mohamed Mursi.

Egypt's military-installed government wavered on appointing Mohamed ElBaradei as interim prime minister, with state media and his office announcing his selection before the government backtracked hours later, saying no final decision had been made.
Hosni Mubarak's retrial for alleged complicity in the killings of 2011 protesters resumed, with his lawyers entering a not guilty plea, and the court adjourned proceedings until August 17.
At least 30 people were killed and 1,076 wounded during violent disturbances in Egypt, according to state television citing Health Ministry sources.
Mohamed ElBaradei is named prime minister of Egypt's new interim government following the military coup against President Mohamed Morsi.

Tens of thousands of anti-Morsi protesters stage a show of force in Cairo's Tahrir Square to back the army's ouster of Egypt's first freely elected president, while Islamist supporters of Morsi hold counter-demonstrations elsewhere in the capital.
An Egyptian court acquits 12 activists opposed to ousted Islamist president Mohamed Morsi of charges they incited violence against members of his Muslim Brotherhood.

Egypt's Islamists call for an "intifada" and vow to keep fighting to restore ousted President Mohammed Morsi to power after protests failed to muster enough strength to challenge the country's military leaders.

Egypt's interim head of state Adli Mansour issued a decree setting a speedy timetable for parliamentary elections within about six months followed by a presidential vote, after the military ouster of President Mohamed Mursi sparked deadly protests.

Anas Mahfous, a 20-year-old Egyptian dental student, was shot in the stomach by a sniper and killed after running toward gunfire to help fellow demonstrators at a sit-in in Cairo demanding the reinstatement of ousted President Mohamed Morsi.

Egyptian security forces opened fire on Muslim Brotherhood supporters outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo, killing at least 51 people, in the worst violence since the military ousted President Mohamed Morsi.

Following a massacre, Egypt's defence chiefs held a press conference showing videos designed to absolve the military of blame, as the country faced what an expert called "a moment of truth" over whether General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi would manage the transition too forcefully or step back behind a civil administration.
Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait pledge $12 billion in aid to Egypt, giving Cairo a window of several months to stabilize its politics and repair its state finances.

Egypt's interim administration names economist Hazem el-Beblawi as Prime Minister and Mohamed ElBaradei as a Vice-President, while the Muslim Brotherhood rejects the appointments and calls for an uprising after more than 51 of its supporters were killed outside the Republican Guard headquarters.
Hazem Beblawi was named Egypt's caretaker prime minister after the first choice for the position was withdrawn due to opposition from Islamists.
The United States cautiously welcomes Egypt's interim government plan to hold quick parliamentary and presidential elections, while avoiding whether a military coup had occurred.
Israeli troops found the remains of a rocket fired from Egypt, the first such rocket since the July 3 overthrow of Egypt's Islamist government.

Egypt's main political players raise objections to a new constitutional decree issued by the military-backed interim authorities, highlighting challenges in reaching consensus to end the crisis and hold new elections.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood rejects a military-backed timetable for fresh elections, saying it brings the country back to square one.
Egypt's Supreme Judicial Council approves the nomination of Hisham Barakat as the new public prosecutor after the resignation of his controversial predecessor, Abdel Meguid Mahmud.
Kuwait, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia pledge a combined $12 billion in aid to Egypt following the military ouster of President Mohammed Morsi.

Egypt's new interim prime minister, Hazem el-Beblawi, began forming a government by meeting liberal politicians Mohamed ElBaradei and Ziad Bahaa el-Din to revive the economy and heal divisions after the army overthrew President Mohamed Mursi.
Egyptian prosecutors issue arrest warrants for Muslim Brotherhood spiritual leader Mohammed Badie and three associates over violence that left at least 51 Morsi supporters dead.
The Egyptian military defends its role in the deaths of at least 51 protesters outside the Republican Guard headquarters in Cairo, saying it used deadly force only after being attacked.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood vows to continue its "peaceful" resistance against the military's ouster of President Mohammed Mursi and demands his release and reinstatement.

Egyptian authorities are holding two Muslim Brotherhood members suspected in the killing of an Alexandria teenager thrown from a rooftop during clashes between supporters and opponents of ousted President Mohamed Morsi.

The U.S. State Department says politically motivated arrests in Egypt, including the public prosecutor's order to arrest Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohamed Badie and other senior Islamists, make it difficult for Egypt to move beyond its political crisis.

Egyptian prosecutors will investigate allegations that ousted president Mohammed Morsi and more than 30 other Muslim Brotherhood leaders escaped from prison during the 2011 revolution with help from Hamas.
Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood calls for new protests after Friday prayers, as the US warns the interim government against "arbitrary arrests" of opposition figures.
Tens of thousands of Islamists rally across Egyptian cities, vowing to sustain for months their campaign to restore deposed President Mohammed Morsi to power.

Supporters and opponents of deposed Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi continue to hold rival rallies in Cairo as the military-backed transitional government moves forward without him or the Muslim Brotherhood.
The Obama administration calls for the release of ousted Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi from military detention, while his supporters vow to continue a sit-in until he is returned to power.
Egypt announces a criminal investigation of deposed president Mohamed Mursi over complaints of spying, inciting violence, and ruining the economy.

Egypt's public prosecutor orders the assets of 14 Muslim Brotherhood members, including its head Mohamed Badie, to be frozen, while army chief Abdel Fattah al-Sisi says no group will be barred from participating in politics.

Mohamed ElBaradei is sworn in as Egypt's interim vice president for foreign relations as a new temporary technocratic government begins to take shape following the military overthrow of President Mohammed Morsy.
Egypt's interim prime minister named senior ministers to his cabinet to lead the country under an army-backed "road map" to restore civil rule.

Egypt's ousted President Mohamed Morsy and several Muslim Brotherhood leaders are being investigated on accusations of killing protesters and spying, while interim Prime Minister Hazem El-Beblawi begins meetings to form a new government.
At least seven people are killed and more than 260 injured in overnight clashes in Cairo between Islamist supporters of deposed president Mohamed Morsi and security forces.

Senior US diplomat William Burns visits Egypt and meets with General Abdel-Fattah al-Sisi and interim leaders, stating Washington supports an inclusive democratic process and does not back any one side.
Unrest in Egypt spills over into a bus attack in Sinai.
Egypt’s U.N. ambassador in Geneva says Egypt wants to reassure the world that the military’s removal of President Mohamed Morsi helps, not hinders, its transition to democracy.
At least seven people were killed and 261 injured in overnight clashes in central Cairo after supporters of deposed President Morsi sparked riots by blocking river crossings.
Egypt's interim President Adly Mahmoud Mansour appoints a new Cabinet of mostly liberals and technocrats, excluding Islamists, as supporters of ousted President Mohamed Morsi clash with police.
The Muslim Brotherhood, facing a crackdown after the military overthrow of President Mohamed Mursi, proposed through an EU go-between a framework for talks.
Britain revoked five export licenses to Egypt to prevent British goods from being used in unrest that has led to civilian deaths.
